html:
SMTO-TSK-0052 — SMTO couldn't carry this conversation into a new one

GUID: 8d6e564e-df65-4f33-9c6a-c3acbfc9003d
Slug: conversation-handoff-invalid
Domain: TSK · Subsystem: tsk

What happened

  • You asked to continue this work in a new conversation, but the saved summary SMTO passes along from the earlier conversation is damaged or in a form it can't use. SMTO couldn't carry that history forward.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Reload the SMTO page and open the conversation you wanted to continue. This makes sure you start from the conversation's current saved state.
  2. On a finished task in that conversation, select ↗ Continue in new conversation. This builds a fresh summary to carry forward instead of reusing the damaged one.
  3. If it fails again, try the same button on a different finished task, or start a new conversation and briefly describe what you were working on. The damaged summary may come from an earlier continuation, so a different starting point can avoid it.

What success looks like

  • A new conversation opens with a "Continued from previous conversation" card at the top.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the name of the original conversation, to the person who manages SMTO. Don't delete the original conversation; it still holds the full history.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Conversation handoff normalization failed: the source conversation's inherited handoff (conversation_handoff_json) is invalid during branch capture, or the handoff passed to a new conversation's first run is invalid during hydration.

What this means

  • Existing/incoming conversation handoff data fails normalization during capture or hydration. Task state and retained ownership decide whether an action is eligible. Diagnostics do not change lane order, consent, snapshots, cancellation or execution; preserve original receipts and reconcile any possible effects before new work.

Why this can happen

  • Existing/incoming conversation handoff data fails normalization during capture or hydration.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect supported handoff version, required fields and ownership without substituting live evidence from another conversation.

How to fix it

  • Inspect the source chat's conversation_handoff_json (and the target's native_handoff_seeds entry) and check why native.conversation_handoff.normalize returns no handoff, for example a missing field or unsupported schema_version. Capture a fresh branch from a task in the source conversation; do not hand-edit the stored handoff.
  • Refresh the source conversation and capture a fresh handoff for the intended target.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • A freshly captured supported handoff normalizes and hydrates in its intended target.

What not to do

  • Do not submit a stale identifier or revision after another actor changed the resource.

Technical notes

  • Task state and retained ownership decide whether an action is eligible. Diagnostics do not change lane order, consent, snapshots, cancellation or execution; preserve original receipts and reconcile any possible effects before new work.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
